ruxen 0.1.3: configuration reload, WebSocket proxying, gzip, access control, rate limiting, a proxy cache, an epoll fallback and a container image. ruxen is an experimental nginx-compatible HTTP server and reverse proxy written from scratch in Rust: Linux-only, HTTP/1.1, thread-per-core on `io_uring` (monoio), TLS via rustls.

> [!WARNING]
> This is an experimental release. It is not production-ready and is not a drop-in replacement for nginx.

Where ruxen is going and in what order: [`ROADMAP.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/main/ROADMAP.md). The short version: an edge server (TLS termination, reverse proxy, static files) that loads nginx configurations as they are. HTTP/2 is next (#144); it is what v0.2.0 waits for.

## Security

No security fixes in this release.

## Behaviour changes

- **Started as root, ruxen now switches to an unprivileged user**, as nginx does: `user` if the configuration sets it, otherwise `nobody` (group `nogroup`, or `nobody` where there is none). Listening sockets and log files are opened as root first. 0.1.2 refused to start as root unless the configuration said `user root;`, which still stays root. Files to be served must be readable by the user ruxen switches to.
- **Where `io_uring` is unavailable, ruxen runs on epoll** instead of refusing to start, and logs one `[notice]` saying why. `RUXEN_DRIVER=io_uring` keeps the old behaviour. epoll is slower on keep-alive traffic (#337).
- **A worker that panics stops the server** (exit status 1, `[alert]` in the error log), so a supervisor restarts it; before, the other workers carried on with fewer listeners. A panic inside one connection ends only that connection.
- **`disable_symlinks off` follows symlinks out of `root` / `alias`**, as nginx does (`html/phpmyadmin -> /usr/share/phpmyadmin`). 0.1.2 answered 403.
- **Redirects carry nginx's page for the status** (`301 Moved Permanently` and the server token) instead of a short stub, and `return 301;` without a URL is a redirect with an empty `Location`, as in nginx.
- **`error_page` no longer intercepts `return <code> "text"`**, as in nginx: the text is sent.
- **A second instance on a busy port** retries `bind()` five times and then fails with nginx's messages.

## Install

Three prebuilt binaries, each also under a versioned name (`ruxen-v0.1.3-<target>.tar.gz`), with a `SHA256SUMS` file:

| tarball | for |
| --- | --- |
| `ruxen-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz` | x86_64 with glibc 2.35 or newer |
| `ruxen-aarch64-linux-gnu.tar.gz` | ARM64 with glibc 2.35 or newer (Graviton, Ampere, Raspberry Pi 5 on a 64-bit OS) |
| `ruxen-x86_64-linux-musl.tar.gz` | any x86_64 Linux, static (Alpine, older glibc) |

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/releases/download/v0.1.3/ruxen-v0.1.3-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS   # after downloading SHA256SUMS from this release
tar xzf ruxen-v0.1.3-x86_64-linux-gnu.tar.gz
cd ruxen-v0.1.3-x86_64-linux-gnu
./ruxen -t -c "$PWD/examples/minimal.conf"
```

**Container image (new)**, amd64 and arm64:

```bash
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 ghcr.io/gvozdetsky/ruxen:0.1.3
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/
```

It runs as an unprivileged user. Docker's default seccomp profile blocks `io_uring`, so under it ruxen runs on epoll; [`contrib/docker/seccomp-io_uring.json`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.1.3/contrib/docker/seccomp-io_uring.json) allows `io_uring` and nothing else beyond the default (`--security-opt seccomp=contrib/docker/seccomp-io_uring.json`). A hardened systemd unit and a logrotate snippet are in [`contrib/`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/tree/v0.1.3/contrib).

From crates.io (needs `cmake` and a C compiler for rustls's `aws-lc-rs` backend):

```bash
cargo install ruxen --locked
```

## What's new since 0.1.2

### Running it

- **Configuration reload** on `SIGHUP` and `ruxen -s reload`: a new generation of workers takes over the same listening sockets, so no connection is refused during the switch. A configuration that fails to load leaves the running one in place. `worker_shutdown_timeout` bounds the old generation. `limit_req` / `limit_conn` zones and a shared `ssl_session_cache` keep their state across reloads.
- **`user`** (see above), with a small root helper for what nginx's master still does as root: reopening logs moved out of root-owned directories, removing the pid file.
- **epoll fallback** (see above).
- **`--compat`** lists everything in a configuration that ruxen doesn't do as nginx: directives it accepts and ignores, and limits.
- `listen unix:/path`, and `unix:` upstream addresses.
- Accept errors are logged and backed off instead of spinning; a panic message always reaches the error log.
- A systemd unit, the container image and a seccomp profile (`contrib/`).

### Reverse proxy

- **WebSocket and other upgraded connections** are tunnelled (`Upgrade`, 101).
- **Response bodies are relayed as they arrive** when they don't come with the header, instead of being buffered whole first (#88, step 1). Server-sent events and slow backends work. A body that arrives with the head, and some cases (`gzip` and `add_trailer` on a relayed body, a cache store, a second pass after `X-Accel-Redirect` or `error_page`), still take the buffered path.
- **A proxy cache:** `proxy_cache_path` (with its loader and manager: `inactive`, `max_size`, `min_free`), `proxy_cache`, `proxy_cache_key`, `proxy_cache_valid`, `proxy_cache_min_uses`, `proxy_cache_methods`, `proxy_cache_bypass` / `proxy_no_cache`, `proxy_ignore_headers`, `proxy_cache_revalidate`, `proxy_cache_use_stale`, `proxy_cache_background_update`, `proxy_cache_lock`, `$upstream_cache_status`. Conditional requests get 304/412 from the cache.
- **`proxy_pass` with variables**, `proxy_bind`, the `hash` and `ip_hash` balancers, `zone` and `max_conns` on upstreams, every address of an upstream host name as a peer.
- `proxy_pass_header Date` keeps the upstream's `Date`. `$document_root`, `$request_filename` and `$uri` in a proxied response's `add_header` have nginx's values.

### HTTP

- **Access control:** `allow`, `deny`, `satisfy` and `limit_except` (they used to be refused at startup).
- **The realip module:** `set_real_ip_from`, `real_ip_header`, `real_ip_recursive`.
- **Rate and connection limits:** `limit_req_zone` / `limit_req`, `limit_conn_zone` / `limit_conn`, shared by all workers.
- **gzip:** `gzip`, `gzip_types`, `gzip_comp_level`, `gzip_vary`, `gzip_min_length`, `gzip_proxied`, `gzip_disable`, … (not yet `gzip_static`, `gunzip`).
- **`stub_status`** and the `$connections_*` variables.
- **`if` inside a location** can hold `proxy_pass`, `add_header`, `root` and the rest, as an anonymous location like nginx's. Nested locations inherit everything nginx merges from the parent.
- Responses of the rewrite phase (`return` in `if`, `rewrite … redirect`) get the location's `add_header` and `error_page`.
- A request that matches no location gets the server's configuration; http-level settings written below a `server` block apply to it; `if ($var = "")` works.
- An `error_page` to a URI continues as GET; a POST to a static file takes `error_page` for its 405.
- `$binary_remote_addr`, `$document_uri`, `$https`, `$arg_NAME` as sent, `$sent_http_*` in `map`.
- `client_body_timeout` and `send_timeout` of the routed location apply.

### Logging and TLS

- `access_log` with `buffer=`, `flush=` and `gzip`, and variables in its path.
- `error_log stderr` keeps stderr; the syslog tag follows the server's identity.
- `ssl_session_ticket_key` (nginx's key files and rotation), `ssl_reject_handshake`.

### Robustness

Fuzzing with `cargo-fuzz`: the request line and headers, `Host`, the URI normaliser, the PROXY protocol header, the chunked request-body decoder, the upstream response head and relayed chunked bodies, and the configuration parser. Overnight runs (about 10.5 billion executions over six targets on 2026-10-14) found no crash.

The full list is the merged pull requests between `v0.1.2` and `v0.1.3`.

### Compatibility

ruxen is checked against the upstream [nginx-tests](https://github.com/nginx/nginx-tests) suite: **106 of the 159 test files** that ruxen opts into pass end-to-end (0.1.2: 65 of 106). The other 346 files are skipped because `ruxen -V` only claims the modules ruxen implements, and this release claims more of them: access, realip, gzip, limit_req, limit_conn, stub_status, upstream hash / ip_hash / zone, and the proxy cache. Per-file status: [`NGINX_TEST_PROGRESS.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.1.3/NGINX_TEST_PROGRESS.md).

Real-world configurations ([`corpus/RESULTS.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.1.3/corpus/RESULTS.md)): **ruxen 0.1.3 loads 193 of the 238 configurations nginx accepts (81%)**; 0.1.2 loaded 149 of 238 (63%).

## Performance

The 0.1.2 campaign was repeated on main a week later: ruxen against nginx 1.24 on the same scenarios, same method (8 interleaved pairs per scenario on the i7 laptop, 6 on the i9, `wrk -t16 -c512` unless noted). It measured main `fce8fa2`. Of the 17 merges after it, each one that touches the request path was measured against its base before merging, and all stayed within the noise floor (±0.5%). The full report: [`bench/campaign-2026-10-14/REPORT.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/v0.1.3/bench/campaign-2026-10-14/REPORT.md).

| | i7-9750H (6 cores, dedicated bench machine) | i9-13900HX (24 cores) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| scenarios | 87 | 71 |
| at ≥ 95% of nginx (the performance contract) | 75 (0.1.2: 64 of 83) | 56 (0.1.2: 54 of 83) |
| ruxen ≥ nginx | 70 | 31 |
| median ruxen / nginx | 118.8% (0.1.2: 109.4%) | 97.8% (0.1.2: 96.9%) |
| clearly better than 0.1.2 / clearly worse | 58 / 0 | 20 / 2 |

On the i9, 18 scenarios that serve generated files are left out: the night checkout had not generated them, so both servers answered 404 (fixed in `pair.sh`, #380). The two worse rows on the i9 are `m1_hello_c4096` (−2.2 points, 95.0%) and `tls12_handshake` (−1.0, 103.6%).

Selected scenarios (ruxen / nginx):

| scenario | i7-9750H | i9-13900HX |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `return 200`, keep-alive (`m1_hello`) | 119.1% | 99.6% |
| static 1 KiB (`m3_static_1k`) | 139.0% | 104.9% |
| reverse proxy, small response (`proxy_hello`) | 120.7% | 97.6% |
| reverse proxy, `X-Accel-Redirect` (`proxy_xar`; 0.1.2: 15.2%) | 112.1% | — |
| reverse proxy, 1 MiB response (`proxy_ext_1m`; 0.1.2: 35.8% / 55.1%) | 94.1% | 142.8% |
| reverse proxy, 64 KiB POST (`proxy_ext_post_64k`; 0.1.2: 55.4% / 93.7%) | 101.6% | 187.4% |
| 50 regex locations (`regex_locations_50`; 0.1.2: 106.2% / 67.9%) | 176.5% | 122.4% |
| autoindex, 100 entries (`autoindex_100`; 0.1.2: 75.7%) | 105.6% | — |
| proxy cache hit (`proxy_cache_hit`) | 135.7% | 110.1% |
| gzip, 8 KiB HTML (`gzip_html_8k`) | 112.4% | 96.1% |
| TLS 1.3, keep-alive (`tls_hello`) | 136.7% | 112.8% |

Still under 95%, each with an issue: a new connection per request (`*_no_keepalive`, 89–95%, #128); 1 MiB responses on the 6-core machine (`m19_stream_1m` 66%, `tls_static_1m` 53%, #247); proxying without upstream keep-alive to a server of the same instance (#249); 64 KiB proxied responses on the 6-core machine (`proxy_64k` 72%, #88); a few variable-heavy scenarios at 91–95% on the i9. On epoll, keep-alive `m1_hello` and `proxy_hello` are at 92–98% of nginx (#337).

## Known limitations

- No HTTP/2 yet ([#144](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/issues/144)).
- `include` does not expand globs (`include conf.d/*.conf;`, [#35](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/issues/35)).
- `proxy_buffering` isn't implemented: a proxied body that arrives together with the response head is still buffered whole before it is sent (up to 64 MiB), see "Reverse proxy" above.
- No variables in `root` / `alias` ([#232](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/issues/232)).
- No TLS to upstream servers (`proxy_pass https://`, #116), no client certificates (`ssl_verify_client on` is refused at startup), no OCSP stapling.
- No `auth_request` (#358), no `proxy_request_buffering off` (#134), no runtime DNS (`resolver`, #133).
- With `sendfile on`, the file side of the transfer is synchronous; `sendfile_max_chunk` is not configurable.
- A reload doesn't free the retired configuration's memory (#343), and can't bind new ports below 1024 after the switch to `user` (#344).
- `-V` reports `nginx version: nginx/1.29.2` (followed by `ruxen version: ruxen/0.1.3`): the nginx-tests harness reads that line and the `configure arguments` to decide which tests apply.

## How to help

- Found a config where nginx and ruxen behave differently, or one that ruxen refuses? Open an issue with the config, the request and both responses.
- Security problems: please report them privately, see [`SECURITY.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
- Setup, tests and benchmarks: [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/gvozdetsky/ruxen/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
